title: Processing and cryopreservation of human ureter tissues for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics assays
protocol: Retrieve ureter tissues from the operating room immediately.
Place the tissue in a container with PBS and keep it on ice.
Wash the tissue with enough PBS to cover it completely in a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the PBS from the centrifuged tissue.
Transfer ureter tissue specimen to a sterile 10 cm tissue culture dish using forceps.
Cut the tissue into pieces approximately 1 cm in length for each separate aliquot of papain if the tissue is large.
Thoroughly mince the tissue at 20°C–25°C until a paste-like consistency is achieved using a sterile blade.
Transfer minced tissue to a 50 mL conical containing 5 mL papain and 500 μL DNase, ensuring enough volume to submerge the tissue.
Wrap cap with parafilm and incubate horizontally with gentle shaking (100 rpm) at 37°C for 1 hour.
Keep the tube horizontal to maintain homogeneity and prevent settling of tissue onto the bottom of the conical tube.
Triturate using a P1000 pipette to check if the tissue is digested, cutting the tip if necessary for chunks.
Add 5.5 ml of ovoid inhibitor to stop the digestion after incubation.
Filter the mixture through a 70 μm cell strainer to remove large debris.
Place a new 70 μm filter onto the top of an open 50 mL conical tube.
Pipette up the cell suspension and expel it slowly through the middle of the filter, avoiding overflow.
Discard the used filter after all mixture has passed through.
Cap the 50 mL conical tube.
Use a sterile pipette tip to move indigestible tissue around the filter to prevent clogging.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C in a rotating bucket centrifuge.
Discard supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend cell pellet in 3 mL ACK lysis buffer and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 3 min.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Carefully discard supernatant.
Transfer the ACK/cell suspension to a new 15 mL conical.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 5 mL PBS at 20°C–25°C, centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C, and carefully discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL of PBS at 20°C–25°C and transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Pass the PBS/cell suspension through a 40 μm Flowmi tip using a p1000 pipette.
Slowly expel the cell mixture into a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Do not go past the first stop on the pipette when expelling the liquid.
Take an aliquot of cells (10 μL).
Mix the aliquot 1:1 with Trypan blue.
Determine cell viability and concentration using Trypan blue mix.
Check the extent of cellular aggregation.
For 10x Genomics scRNA-seq, ensure minimal cell clumps.
Pass the sample through a new Flowmi tip if substantial clumps are present.
Optionally add BSA to PBS at a concentration of 0.04%–2% to decrease aggregation and minimize cell loss.
Keep cells in PBS on ice for up to 30 min until ready for scRNA-seq or other downstream applications.
Determine the total number of cells to cryopreserve.
Approximate the best volume of freezing media to use based on cell count.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of freezing media for up to 1 million cells.
For more than 1 million cells, keep a concentration of 1 million/mL in freezing media.
Prepare the correct number of labeled cryovials.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the appropriate volume of freezing media.
Aliquot into the pre-determined number of cryovials for freezing.
Quickly transfer vials of cells into a Styrofoam box or an isopropanol cooler.
Place the vials in the -80°C freezer.
Remove desired number of vials from the −80°C freezer.
Transfer the vial quickly to a 37°C water bath.
Resuspend thawed cells in 10 mL of pre-warmed DMEM/F-12 media supplemented with 10% FBS and transfer liquid to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Gently remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 10 mL of PBS and centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash cells by gently removing supernatant after resuspension in PBS.
Depend on downstream application to resuspend the cell pellet in 250 μL-1 mL of PBS and keep on ice.
Take a 10 μL aliquot of cell suspension and mix 1:1 with Trypan blue for viability assessment.
Take a horizontal cross section of the ureter approximately 5 mm in length and typically less than 0.5 cm in width.
Rinse the tissue in PBS.
Gently pick up the tissue using non-toothed forceps.
Wick off excess moisture using a paper towel.
Obtain a pre-labeled cryomold.
Fill halfway with O.C.T., being careful not to introduce any bubbles.
Place ureter tissue in the middle of the O.C.T./cryomold.
Cover the ureter tissue with additional O.C.T. to fill the mold completely.
Transfer the filled cryomold to the pre-chilled isopentane bath for freezing.
Check that the isopentane is sufficiently cold by adding a small piece of dry ice and observing no bubbles or boiling.
Observe the O.C.T. turning opaque white, indicating complete freezing of the sample.
Wrap the frozen sample in aluminum foil once fully opaque.
Place the wrapped samples in dry ice until ready for transfer to the −80°C freezer.
Seal the foil-wrapped samples in a plastic bag.
Transfer sealed samples to a pre-chilled box in the −80°C freezer.
